Hi Chloe / Marissa,

Thanks again — procurement has a couple of checklist items we can’t close without a short note from engineering about how you measure uptime and latency SLOs, and whether BrightWave can get short-term access to metrics while we finish onboarding. Attached is our standard procurement questionnaire (procurement_questionnaire.pdf) — questions 4–7 are the ones holding us up.

Top asks from procurement:
- Exact SLO definitions (what counts as an incident / downtime).
- Which latency buckets you measure (p50/p95/p99) and whether these are per-route or aggregated.
- Monitoring/alerting cadence and who gets alerted.
- Whether BrightWave can be granted read-only dashboard access for 30–60 days while integration completes.

Can you confirm the answers and whether Redwood can provide a temporary dashboard carveout? We’d prefer a short written response we can attach to the SR. Procurement is on a tight deadline — can you get back by EOD Friday?

Appreciate it,

Subject: Re: Procurement: SLO measurement & temporary metrics access request

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. Looping in Karthik from Reliability to confirm instrumentation details. Below is an actionable summary you can drop into procurement:

Summary of measurement & access (short form)
- Uptime SLO: service-level "availability" is measured as successful 5xx-free responses per route over a rolling 30d window; target = 99.95% per-customer (route-level for pinned model endpoints). Incident definition: any 5xx spike or sustained error rate >1% for 5 minutes that impacts customer requests.
- Latency SLOs: we record p50/p95/p99 per-route and per-model-variant on a 5-minute sampling window. Typical target: p95 <= 250ms for small-context text generation routes; p99 <= 800ms for long-context or heavy-engine routes — we publish per-model profiles in our catalog.
- Measurement notes: metrics are computed from server-side telemetry (request latencies, error codes, and sequence-length-normalized token counts). To avoid noisy signals, we use a sampling policy for very-high-volume customers (1–5% sampling at high throughput) — sampling is documented and included in reports.
- Monitoring & alerting: on-call/ops receive automated alerts for SLO burn rates and incident thresholds; Sev-1 triggers on sustained downtime or error-rate thresholds, sent to ops@redwood.ai and on-call Slack channel. Customer-facing incident updates are posted to status.redwood.ai.
- Customer access to metrics: we can provide read-only Grafana dashboards scoped to your account (time-limited), plus periodic CSV exports. Dashboards include p50/p95/p99, error rates, and token throughput. Sampling caveat: very-high-volume routes may show aggregated/sampled values and we annotate that on the dashboard.

Temporary carveout proposal
- Duration: 45 days (to cover full integration + handover).
- Scope: read-only dashboard + scheduled CSV exports (daily) for the requested metrics; no access to raw logs or internal traces.
- Controls: access via RBAC account linked to your SSO; IP restriction option available on request; access revoked automatically at end of window.

Next steps
- If that works, we’ll prepare a short amendment (DocuSign) that procurement can sign. I’ve attached a sample export we can provide (slo-evidence-sample.csv).
- Karthik: can you confirm the incident definition wording and the sampling percentages for enterprise-high-throughput customers?

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
